title: Finite coherent diagram shapes generated by initial objects and pushouts
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be an infinity category, modeled by a simplicial set with fillers for every inner horn $\Lambda^n_k\subseteq\Delta^n$, $0<k<n$. Here $\Delta^n$ is the nerve of the ordered set $\{0<\cdots<n\}$, and $\Lambda^n_k$ is the union of its codimension-one faces except the $k$th face [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set]. A finite diagram means a map $K\to\mathcal C$ where $K$ has finitely many nondegenerate simplices. A colimit means an initial object in the infinity category of cocones, equivalently an object representing the space of coherent cocones by its mapping spaces; a limit is defined dually. Then $\mathcal C$ admits colimits of all finite diagrams if and only if it has an initial object and all pushouts. Dually it admits limits of all finite diagrams if and only if it has a terminal object and all pullbacks. In these assertions the objects, squares and universal properties are infinity categorical, not limits in the ordinary homotopy category.

source.place: Lurie, Higher Topos Theory, Proposition 4.4.2.2 and Corollary 4.4.2.4 (finite simplicial sets, including the empty set); the limit assertion is the same corollary applied to the opposite infinity category. Read online; not archived in the shared literature/. Stacks Categories Lemma 002O (lemma-finite-limits-exist) is only the ordinary-category analogue.

proof.text: For necessity, the empty simplicial set is finite, and its cocone category is $\mathcal C$ itself, so its colimit is an initial object. The nerve of the three-object span $b\leftarrow a\to c$ has three nondegenerate vertices and two nondegenerate edges and no other nondegenerate simplices; its colimits are exactly pushouts. Thus all finite colimits supply the two asserted special cases. The same argument with cones gives terminal objects and pullbacks from all finite limits.

source.place: HTT Corollary 4.4.2.4, proof, with Proposition 4.4.2.2; online, not archived. Agent expansion of the simplicial attachment and duality details.

proof.text: For sufficiency assume an initial object and all pushouts. Prove, for every finite simplicial set $K$ and every $p:K\to\mathcal C$, that $p$ has a colimit. Induct first on the dimension (put $\dim\varnothing=-1$), then, for fixed dimension $n\geq0$, on the positive number of nondegenerate $n$-simplices. All lower-dimensional shapes are available in the outer induction. The empty diagram has the assumed initial object as colimit. Finiteness guarantees a largest dimension whenever $K$ is nonempty.

source.place: HTT Corollary 4.4.2.4, proof, with Proposition 4.4.2.2; online, not archived. Agent expansion of the simplicial attachment and duality details.

proof.text: Choose a nondegenerate $n$-simplex $\sigma$ of maximal dimension. Define $K_0\subseteq K$ by removing exactly the simplices whose unique nondegenerate ancestor is $\sigma$, using [lem-weil-pbc-simplicial-set-nondegenerate-decomposition]. This is a simplicial subset: if an operator applied to a simplex rooted at $\tau\neq\sigma$ had ancestor $\sigma$, factor its composite ordinal map into a surjection followed by an injection. If that injection is proper its face has dimension less than $\dim\tau\leq n$ and cannot have the $n$-dimensional ancestor $\sigma$; if it is an identity, uniqueness of ancestors forces $\tau=\sigma$. Thus operators preserve $K_0$. For any simplex $z\in K_0$ with decomposition $z=K(q)(\tau)$ for a surjection $q$, an order-preserving section $i$ of $q$ gives $\tau=K(i)(z)\in K_0$. Consequently a simplex of $K_0$ is nondegenerate there if and only if it is nondegenerate in $K$. Thus $K_0$ is finite, has all the simplices below degree $n$, exactly one fewer nondegenerate $n$-simplex, and no nondegenerate simplices above degree $n$. In degree $n$ the only surjective endomorphism of $[n]$ is the identity, so $K_n=(K_0)_n\cup\{\sigma\}$. The inclusion $K_0\subseteq K$ satisfies all three hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-simplicial-set-glue-simplex], which gives $K=K_0\amalg_{\partial\Delta^n}\Delta^n$. Here $\partial\Delta^n$ consists of nonsurjective ordinal maps into $[n]$, and its map into $\Delta^n$ is degreewise injective; its map into $K_0$ may identify faces.

source.place: Lemma 017R (lemma-splitting-simplicial-sets) and Lemma 018R (lemma-glue-simplex); agent construction of the complement of a maximal nondegenerate simplex, as in HTT Corollary 4.4.2.4.

proof.text: The shape $K_0$ is finite and either has dimension less than $n$ or has dimension $n$ and fewer top simplices, so its restricted diagram has a colimit $X$ by induction. The nondegenerate simplices of $\partial\Delta^n$ are the injective nonsurjective ordinal maps into $[n]$: there are finitely many, all of dimension less than $n$. Hence the boundary diagram has a colimit $Y$ by the outer induction; for $n=0$ it is empty and $Y$ is the initial object. Write $a:\Delta^n\to K$ for the simplex map furnished in Step 3. Apply the explicit standard-simplex clause of [lem-coef-infinity-final-index-colimit] to $p\circ a$, obtaining its colimit $Z=p(a(n))$. Its cocone is the composite of $p\circ a$ with the order map $[n+1]\to[n]$ fixing $0,\ldots,n$ and sending $n+1$ to $n$; the edge at the final vertex is an identity, including when $n=0$.

source.place: HTT Corollary 4.4.2.4, proof, with Proposition 4.4.2.2; online, not archived. Agent expansion of the simplicial attachment and duality details.

proof.text: The chosen cocones of $X,Y,Z$ induce the coherent span $X\leftarrow Y\to Z$. It has a pushout $P$ by the hypothesis on $\mathcal C$. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-colimit-gluing] to the indexing pushout of Step 3 and these three colimit cocones: its monomorphism hypothesis is precisely $\partial\Delta^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$, irrespective of identifications in the attaching map into $K_0$. It supplies a colimit cocone for $p$ with vertex $P$. This proves the inner inductive step (including the last top simplex, when $K_0$ falls to lower dimension), and hence both inductions.

source.place: HTT Corollary 4.4.2.4, proof, with Proposition 4.4.2.2; online, not archived. Agent expansion of the simplicial attachment and duality details.

proof.text: For the limit sufficiency, take opposites. Explicitly reverse every ordinal: replace $\alpha:[m]\to[n]$ by $\alpha^{\mathrm{rev}}(i)=n-\alpha(m-i)$ and precompose a simplicial set with this involution. It exchanges inner horns $\Lambda^n_k$ with $\Lambda^n_{n-k}$, so $\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}}$ is again an infinity category, and preserves the number and dimensions of nondegenerate simplices. Reversing a coherent cone over $p:K\to\mathcal C$ gives a coherent cocone over $p^{\mathrm{op}}:K^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}}$, with arrows and all higher simplices reversed; reversing twice is the identity. Thus terminal objects become initial objects, pullback universal properties become pushout universal properties, and colimit cocones become limit cones. Apply the colimit sufficiency just proved to $\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}}$ and each finite $K^{\mathrm{op}}$, then reverse back. This proves the limit assertion using coherent universal properties throughout.
